title: The Umbrella That Wasn't There
scene: At a small art museum, you listen to an audio guide that keeps describing a red umbrella. The painting in front of you shows only a blue sea. After puzzling over it, you discover you selected the wrong track.
sceneJa: 小さな美術館で音声ガイドを聞いていると、赤い傘の説明が続く。しかし目の前の絵は青い海。自分の鑑賞眼を疑いかけたところで、再生番号を間違えたと気づく。最後のガイドの一言が、妙に自分への助言に聞こえる。

chunks.en: I was halfway through the museum's audio guide
chunks.ja: 美術館の音声ガイドを半分ほど聞いたところで

chunks.en: the painting didn't match the description.
chunks.ja: 絵と説明が合っていないことに

chunks.en: The narrator kept mentioning a bright red umbrella,
chunks.ja: ナレーターは鮮やかな赤い傘の話を繰り返していたのに
穏やかな青い海だけだった

chunks.en: I couldn't make sense of it,
so I stood there for another minute,
chunks.ja: さらに1分ほどその場に立ったまま
何を見落としているのか考えていた

chunks.en: I checked the number beside the frame
chunks.ja: 額の横にある番号を確認すると

chunks.en: and found I'd selected track sixteen instead of nineteen.
chunks.ja: 19番ではなく16番を選んでいたと分かった

chunks.en: By the time I switched to the right track,
chunks.ja: 正しい音声に切り替えた頃には

chunks.en: searching for an umbrella in the ocean.
chunks.ja: 海の中に傘を探すことに
新しい音声はこう始まった
「水面の穏やかさに注目してください」
妙に自分への助言のように聞こえた

questions.question: Which grouping keeps 'all I could see' as a meaningful unit?
options: but all I / could see was / a calm blue sea.
but all I could see / was a calm blue sea.
but all / I could see was a / calm blue sea.
questions.explanation: 'All I could see' means the only thing visible to the speaker. Keep the expression together, then add what they could see.

questions.question: What does 'I couldn't make sense of it' mean here?
options: The speaker couldn't understand why the description didn't fit.
The speaker couldn't hear the audio guide at all.
The speaker couldn't find the museum exit.
questions.explanation: 'Make sense of something' means to understand it. The speaker cannot reconcile the umbrella description with the blue sea.

questions.question: Why does the final line sound like advice to the speaker?
options: The guide knew the speaker had chosen the wrong track.
The guide was telling visitors to leave the museum.
After overthinking the mix-up, the speaker hears 'calm' as an amusing reminder to relax.
questions.explanation: The recording is describing the painting, not addressing the speaker. The joke comes from the speaker's self-conscious interpretation.

speak: Imagine misunderstanding a museum label, sign, instruction, or announcement. Imagine: you are looking at a calm seascape while the guide describes a red umbrella. Read: read all six sentences aloud once. Chunk: pause after 'I was halfway through the museum's audio guide', 'all I could see', and 'Just to make sure'. Understand: 'make sense of' means understand, and 'all I could see' limits what was visible. Check: answer the three questions. Speak: for 30 seconds, describe a time a description did not match what you saw. Use 'I was halfway through ...', 'I couldn't make sense of it', and 'Just to make sure, I ...'. Read aloud again: slow down for the final sentence and deliver it with gentle self-deprecating humour. Final Read: read all six sentences smoothly without looking at the Japanese.
review: New chunks: 'I was halfway through ...' (〜の途中まで進んだところだった), 'all I could see was ...' (見えるのは〜だけだった), 'I couldn't make sense of it' (どうにも理解できなかった). Reuse Lesson 92 'Just to make sure' (念のため) in a museum instead of a meeting-place clarification. Reuse Lesson 90 'By the time ...' (〜する頃には) to describe time wasted rather than a football match. Pragmatics: 'sounded suspiciously like advice' is playful, not a claim that the recording actually addressed the narrator.
